title: Canonical infinitesimal fibre cohomology system and stalk restrictions
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], $y\in Y$, $\mathcal F$ an $\mathcal O_X$-module, and $p\ge0$. Put $A=\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ and $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak m_y$. At index $n\in\mathbb N$ put $c_n:\operatorname{Spec}(A/\mathfrak m^{n+1})\to\operatorname{Spec}A\to Y$ and $X_n=\operatorname{Spec}(A/\mathfrak m^{n+1})\times_YX$ [def-pc-fibre-product], with projection $i_n:X_n\to X$ and $\mathcal F_n=i_n^*\mathcal F$ [def-pc-module-pullback]. Let $j_n:X_n\to X_{n+1}$ be the base change of the reduction $\operatorname{Spec}(A/\mathfrak m^{n+1})\to\operatorname{Spec}(A/\mathfrak m^{n+2})$ (the map induced on fibre products by it and $\mathrm{id}_X$), so $i_{n+1}\circ j_n=i_n$. The cohomology $H_n=H^p(X_n,\mathcal F_n)$ [pqf-def-cohomology] is an $A/\mathfrak m^{n+1}$-module through $\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}(A/\mathfrak m^{n+1}),\mathcal O)\to\Gamma(X_n,\mathcal O)$, hence an $A$-module and an $\widehat A$-module via evaluation $\widehat A\to A/\mathfrak m^{n+1}$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. The transition $H_{n+1}\to H_n$ is the cohomology map [def-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap] of the $j_n$-map $\mathcal F_{n+1}\to j_{n*}\mathcal F_n$ adjoint (for $i_{n+1}^*\dashv i_{n+1,*}$) to the unit $\mathcal F\to i_{n*}\mathcal F_n=i_{n+1,*}j_{n*}\mathcal F_n$, i.e. the adjoint of the canonical identification $j_n^*\mathcal F_{n+1}\cong\mathcal F_n$; it is $\widehat A$-linear, and these maps form an inverse system of $\widehat A$-modules. Put $M=(R^pf_*\mathcal F)_y$, the module stalk [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk], [def-pc-module-stalk-functor]. An $A$-linear map $\theta_n:M\to H_n$ is the *canonical stalk map* if for every open $V\ni y$ and every class $\xi\in H^p(f^{-1}V,\mathcal F|_{f^{-1}V})$ it sends the germ at $y$ of the canonical image of $\xi$ in $(R^pf_*\mathcal F)(V)$ [lem-weil-pbc-higher-direct-image-presheaf] (computed by restricted injective resolutions, [def-weil-pbc-flat-base-change-open-choices]) to the class whose restriction to $i_n^{-1}(f^{-1}V)=X_n$ is the pullback of $\xi$ along $i_n^{-1}(f^{-1}V)\to f^{-1}V$ [def-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap]; since germs of such images exhaust $M$ and this restriction is an isomorphism, there is at most one such map. In degree zero for $\mathcal F=\mathcal O_X$, also form the inverse system of the actual section modules $\Gamma(X_n,\mathcal O_{X_n})$, with the same scalar actions and the section pullbacks along $j_n$ as transitions.

proof.text: formalFibreBaseMap_transition follows from contravariant functoriality of Spec and the quotient-factor equation; formalFibreTransition_ι follows from the second projection equation for pullback.map, as in the previously landed proof.
proof.elementary: Functoriality, quotient factorization, and pullback projection equations in Mathlib.

proof.text: Prove compatibility of the scalar maps with reduction: the first projection equation for pullback.map gives j_n followed by the first projection equal to the first projection followed by Spec of the quotient reduction. Apply appTop and naturality of Scheme.ΓSpecIso.inv to obtain scalarMap_transition. On a Cauchy-sequence representative of an element of the completion, AdicCompletion.evalₐ_mk and AdicCompletion.Ideal.mk_eq_mk show that factorPow composed with evaluation at n+2 is evaluation at n+1. Combine these identities to prove completedScalarMap_transition.
proof.elementary: Pullback projection equations, naturality of the Gamma-Spec isomorphism, and the defining compatibility of completion evaluations; all supplied by Mathlib.

proof.text: Use clause (1) of the h-map basic properties to obtain a global-sections-linear map with the specified underlying additive cohomology map. Its map_smul equation gives cohomologyFMap_smul. Specialize to j_n and the canonical transition h-map, and rewrite completedScalarMap_transition. Restriction of scalars unfolds to give formalFibreCohomologyTransition_smul.

For actual global sections, unfold the restricted scalar actions into multiplication by the image of the completed scalar. Apply map_mul for j_n.appTop.hom and completedScalarMap_transition to prove formalFibreSectionsTransition_smul. The existing linear-map and inverse-system definitions then require no remaining proof holes in this module.
proof.elementary: Multiplicativity of a ring homomorphism and the scalar compatibility proved above.
